front.title: RSASSA-PSS with SHA-256 under an RSA private key

abstract.t: A profile of RFC 8017 for nish/crypto/rsa-sign: an RSA private key read from PKCS #1's RSAPrivateKey, the RSASP1 primitive under it, and RSASSA-PSS signing with SHA-256 and MGF1 with SHA-256, the TLS 1.3 scheme rsa_pss_rsae_sha256 of RFC 8446. Every requirement quotes RFC 8017, the main source, or RFC 8446; every binding sentence of RFC 8017 (MUST, MUST NOT, SHALL, SHALL NOT, REQUIRED) is tested or excluded here.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

nish/crypto/rsa-sign reads a two-prime RSAPrivateKey (RFC 8017 Section A.1.2) of 2048 to 4096 bits from the bytes [start, end) of an array and holds it as a Secret; the properties see that Secret as bytes, and pass it back as they got it. rsaSignRaw is RSASP1 (Section 5.2.1) on a k-octet big-endian message representative, k the modulus's length in octets. rsaSignPssSha256Salted is RSASSA-PSS-SIGN (Section 8.1.1) with EMSA-PSS-ENCODE (Section 9.1.1) over SHA-256, MGF1 with SHA-256 and the salt the caller gives; rsaSignPssSha256 derives a 32-octet salt (below). Parsing and signing return null on any failure. rsaVerifyPssDer, from nish/crypto/rsa, is RSASSA-PSS-VERIFY under a PKCS #1 RSAPublicKey (Section A.1.1) with the hash it is told (1 is SHA-256) and the salt length it is told; it is the independent check every signing property uses.

Every property signs under one fixed RSA-2048 key, written out as its DER in each property, made by OpenSSL 3.0.13 (openssl genrsa 2048), and its public key, openssl rsa -RSAPublicKey_out -outform DER. The two known answers are OpenSSL's too: P-PSS-KNOWN is openssl pkeyutl -sign -rawin -digest sha256 -pkeyopt rsa_padding_mode:pss -pkeyopt rsa_pss_saltlen:0 over "sample", and P-RAW-KNOWN is openssl rsautl -sign -raw over the 256 octets 00 to ff, also checked against a square-and-multiply in BigInt.

Out of scope: rsaSignPssSha256Into, the same signature as rsaSignPssSha256 written into a caller's array through an RsaSignScratch, held by tests/link/crypto_rsa_sign; its first parameter is the class RsaSignScratch, which a ts-interface block refuses

Out of scope: rsaSignPssSha256SaltedInto, the same signature as rsaSignPssSha256Salted written into a caller's array through an RsaSignScratch, held by tests/link/crypto_rsa_sign; its first parameter is the class RsaSignScratch, which a ts-interface block refuses
Out of scope: RsaSignScratch, the reusable scratch of the two Into signers, a class and not a function
Out of scope: RSA_SIGN_MIN_BITS, an i32 constant a property cannot call; every property reads a 2048-bit key, which is that minimum
Out of scope: RSA_SIGN_MAX_BITS, an i32 constant a property cannot call; a 4096-bit key is held by tests/link/crypto_rsa_sign
Out of scope: RSA_PSS_SHA256_SALT_SIZE, an i32 constant a property cannot call; P-SALT-DERIVED holds the 32-octet salt

section.name: Interface
section.sourcecode: // module: nish/crypto/rsa-sign export const rsaParsePrivateKey = (der: u8[], start: i32, end: i32): Secret<u8[]> | null export const rsaPrivateKeyBits = (priv: Secret<u8[]>): i32 export const rsaPrivateKeyModulus = (priv: Secret<u8[]>): u8[] export const rsaPrivateKeyExponent = (priv: Secret<u8[]>): u8[] export const rsaSignRaw = (priv: Secret<u8[]>, m: u8[]): u8[] | null export const rsaSignPssSha256Salted = (priv: Secret<u8[]>, msg: u8[], salt: u8[]): u8[] | null export const rsaSignPssSha256 = (priv: Secret<u8[]>, msg: u8[]): u8[] | null // module: nish/crypto/rsa export const rsaVerifyPssDer = (der: u8[], hash: i32, saltLen: i32, msg: u8[], sig: u8[]): boolean // module: nish/crypto/sha256 export const sha256 = (data: u8[]): u8[]

blockquote.t: In a valid RSA private key with the first representation, the RSA modulus n is the same as in the corresponding RSA public key and is the product of u distinct odd primes r_i, i = 1, 2, ..., u, where u >= 2.
The RSA private exponent d is a positive integer less than n satisfying

In a valid RSA private key with the second representation, the two factors p and q are the first two prime factors of the RSA modulus n (i.e., r_1 and r_2); the CRT exponents dP and dQ are positive integers less than p and q, respectively, satisfying
and the CRT coefficient qInv is a positive integer less than p satisfying
It SHALL be 0 for this version of the document, unless multi-prime is used; in which case, it SHALL be 1.
It SHALL be omitted if version is 0 and SHALL contain at least one instance of OtherPrimeInfo if version is 1.
Version ::= INTEGER { two-prime(0), multi(1) } (CONSTRAINED BY {-- version MUST be multi if otherPrimeInfos present --})
If the message representative m is not between 0 and n - 1, output "message representative out of range" and stop.
Let s_1 = m^dP mod p and s_2 = m^dQ mod q.
Let h = (s_1 - s_2) * qInv mod p.
Let s = s_2 + q * h.
EM = EMSA-PSS-ENCODE (M, modBits - 1).
S = I2OSP (s, k).
If emLen < hLen + sLen + 2, output "encoding error" and stop.
Let mHash = Hash(M), an octet string of length hLen.
Generate a random octet string salt of length sLen; if sLen = 0, then salt is the empty string.
Let DB = PS || 0x01 || salt; DB is an octet string of length emLen - hLen - 1.
Let EM = maskedDB || H || 0xbc.
The length of the Salt MUST be equal to the length of the output of the digest algorithm.

section.name: Out of Scope
section.t: RFC 8017 prints no RSA key, signature or intermediate value, so this profile has no vectors: every clause is a property over the fixed key the Introduction names, and the two known answers are OpenSSL's, checked as properties.

nish/crypto/rsa-sign derives the salt of rsaSignPssSha256 where Section 9.1.1 step 4 generates a random one: the SHA-256 of the octets of "nish rsa-pss-sha256 salt", the private exponent d as k big-endian octets, and mHash. Note 4 of Section 8.1 keeps a security reduction for any salt, the empty one included, and a verifier cannot tell a derived salt from a drawn one. P-SALT-DERIVED holds the derivation, and P-SALTED holds that any salt the caller gives is encoded as step 4 says.
Multi-prime keys (version 1, Section 3.2's triplets r_i, d_i, t_i and the steps 2.b.2 and 2.b.5 of Section 5.2.1) are refused, not implemented: P-KEY-VERSION holds the refusal.

Keys below 2048 bits or above 4096 bits are refused, and so is a key whose p or q is longer than half the modulus rounded up to 32 bits; RFC 8017 sets no size, and the keys OpenSSL, Go and BoringSSL generate have primes of half the modulus's bits.

RSASSA-PSS-VERIFY (Section 8.1.2), RSAES (Section 7), RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 (Section 8.2) and the ASN.1 of the algorithm identifiers (Appendix A.2) are nish/crypto/rsa's or not implemented. rsaVerifyPssDer is the check here, not a function under test.

Sections 5.2.1 and 8.1 ask for no defence against timing or faults in binding words. nish/crypto/rsa-sign computes with the secret values in constant time, held by tests/cases/ct_asm_rsa.ts, and raises every signature to e and compares it with the message representative before it returns it, against the fault that factors n from one faulty CRT half (docs/security/crypto-rsa.md, RSA-S2). Neither is observable by a functional test.

section.name: Properties

abstract.t: This document provides recommendations for the implementation of public-key cryptography based on the RSA algorithm, covering cryptographic primitives, encryption schemes, signature schemes with appendix, and ASN.1 syntax for representing keys and for identifying the schemes.
This document represents a republication of PKCS #1 v2.2 from RSA Laboratories' Public-Key Cryptography Standards (PKCS) series. By publishing this RFC, change control is transferred to the IETF.

front.title: The Transport Layer Security (TLS) Protocol Version 1.3

abstract.t: This document specifies version 1.3 of the Transport Layer Security (TLS) protocol. TLS allows client/server applications to communicate over the Internet in a way that is designed to prevent eavesdropping, tampering, and message forgery.
This document updates RFCs 5705 and 6066, and obsoletes RFCs 5077, 5246, and 6961. This document also specifies new requirements for TLS 1.2 implementations.

front.title: Key words for use in RFCs to Indicate Requirement Levels

abstract.t: In many standards track documents several words are used to signify the requirements in the specification. These words are often capitalized. This document defines these words as they should be interpreted in IETF documents. This document specifies an Internet Best Current Practices for the Internet Community, and requests discussion and suggestions for improvements.

front.title: Ambiguity of Uppercase vs Lowercase in RFC 2119 Key Words

abstract.t: RFC 2119 specifies common key words that may be used in protocol specifications. This document aims to reduce the ambiguity by clarifying that only UPPERCASE usage of the key words have the defined special meanings.
